title: Identify Equivalent Algebraic Expressions · Part 2
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can show that two expressions are equivalent by simplifying and combining like terms.
languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words equivalent, simplify, like terms, and combine.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that look different but have the same value for every allowed variable value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que se ven diferentes pero tienen el mismo valor para cada valor permitido de la variable.
vocabulary.cloze: Expressions with the same value for ___ allowed number are equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that always have the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que siempre tienen el mismo valor.
vocabulary.visual: 2x + 4 and 2(x + 2): when x = 3, both = 10; when x = 7, both = 18 — always the same

examples.why: Equal for every value of x.
They differ once x is anything but 1.

vocabulary.cloze: Expressions that always have the same value are ___.

vocabulary.definition: To rewrite an expression in a shorter form that is still equal to the original.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una expresión en una forma más corta que sigue siendo igual a la original.
vocabulary.visual: 3x + 2x + 5 simplifies to 5x + 5 — fewer terms, same value
vocabulary.cloze: Rewriting an expression in a shorter form that is still equal to it is to ___ it.

examples.why: The two x-terms combine; the value is unchanged.
The 5 is not an x-term, so it cannot join them.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.
vocabulary.visual: 3x and 7x are like terms (both x); 3x and 3y are NOT (x vs y); 3x and 3x² are NOT (x vs x²)
vocabulary.cloze: Terms with the same variable raised to the same power, like 4x and 9x, are ___.

examples.why: Both have the same variable x to the first power.
One has a variable and one does not, so they are not like terms.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar o restar términos con la misma letra en uno solo.
vocabulary.visual: 4n + 3n = 7n — add the coefficients (4 + 3 = 7) and keep the variable (n)
vocabulary.cloze: To add or subtract like terms into one term is to ___ them.

examples.why: A constant cannot join a variable term.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número frente a una letra, como el 3 en 3x.
vocabulary.visual: In 5x + 3, the coefficient of x is 5 — when x = 2, the 5x part equals 10
vocabulary.cloze: A number multiplied by a variable is a ___.

items.meaning: Expressions that always have the same value
To rewrite an expression in a shorter form

steps: 1. Equivalent expressions produce the same value for any substitution of the variable
2. Simplify expressions using algebraic properties (Distributive, Commutative, Associative)
3. Test equivalence by substituting two different test numbers

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bonus Points
revealWordProblem.text:
Anwar's quiz bowl team must correctly answer the question shown on the screen to earn ten bonus points in their match. The question is: How can you determine if two expressions are equivalent? Describe how to do this in your own words.
Question: How should Anwar's team respond if they want to earn the ten bonus points?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A projector screen headed Quiz Bowl, asking how you can determine if two expressions are equivalent.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: A complete answer names two ways and says why they agree. First, simplify both expressions using the properties of operations — combine like terms and use the distributive property — and see whether they reduce to the same expression, as 3x + 2x + 10 and 5x + 10 both do. Second, substitute the same value for the variable into each expression and check that both give the same result; testing several values makes the check stronger. Equivalent expressions give the same value for every value of the variable, so a single substitution can suggest equivalence but only simplifying proves it.

choiceFeedback: Both have the same variable x. Add the coefficients: 4 + 3 = 7.
hints: 4x and 3x share the exact same variable, x — that makes them like terms.
Combine like terms by adding the coefficients (the number parts). The variable tags along unchanged.
Add the coefficients: 4 + 3. Keep the x exactly as it is — no new exponent appears.
hintsEs: 4x y 3x comparten exactamente la misma variable, x: eso los hace términos semejantes.
Combina términos semejantes sumando los coeficientes (la parte numérica). La variable se queda igual.
Suma los coeficientes: 4 + 3. Conserva la x tal cual: no aparece ningún exponente nuevo.
